lead: Since 2020, private Indian companies have been allowed to build rockets and satellites. This page shows who they are, what they have really done, and how much India's space business could grow.
try: Under Who does what, tap Skyroot Aerospace, then Pixxel. Then press Goal pace on the growth chart.
points: In July 2026, Skyroot's Vikram-1 became the first rocket built by a private Indian company to reach orbit.
Startup satellites already in space can spot sick crops, see through monsoon clouds and track space junk.
India's goal is to grow its space business about five times, from $8.4 billion in 2022 to $44 billion by 2033. That needs about 16% growth every single year.
